key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Rapid onset within hours to days of inciting event. LOCATION: Bilateral lung fields, diffuse. DURATION: Persistent, requires mechanical ventilation. CHARACTER: Severe dyspnea, air hunger, 'drowning sensation'. AGGRAVATING: Any exertion, lying flat. RELIEVING: High-flow oxygen, mechanical ventilation, prone positioning. TIMING: Continuous, progressive. SEVERITY: Severe (8-10/10), life-threatening. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Tachypnea, tachycardia, cyanosis, altered mental status, multi-organ failure. KEY POSITIVES: Severe dyspnea, bilateral infiltrates on CXR, refractory hypoxemia. KEY NEGATIVES: No chest pain, no wheezing (unless underlying asthma).
